property.value: tilelang-mlir-ascend: AbsFwdOp/autotune_2d (intent=unit_test, kernel=testing/autotune/abs/abs_2d.py): tilelang-mlir-ascend cannot be raced in-process: its Python package is also called `tilelang` and its build/libtilelang.so shares our soname, so importing it here would either shadow or collide with the tilelang that compiled the tested side (D042/R272 -- STB_GNU_UNIQUE, and neither RTLD_LOCAL nor DEEPBIND gets out of it). Handing _race a placeholder callable is not an alternative, and T289 measured what actually happens rather than predicting it: the D032 timer REFUSES a block that emits no device kernel (devicetimer.py:344, 'produced no device kernel'), and because _race puts every candidate in ONE session, that exception takes the whole selection session down -- the other candidates lose their measurement too. (R278 section 6.1 predicted a ~0 us candidate being elected as infinitely fast; the direction was right, the mechanism was not -- the timer's guard fires first. R289-data/02-counterfactual.json.) This baseline is measured out of process by baselines._b_tl_mlir.measure_case(); see docs/reports/R278.md. MEASURED ELSEWHERE, NOT MISSING: docs/reports/R282-data/22-timing-summary.json (34 cases x N=5 cross-process, D032 timer, bias band 3.2051%) and docs/reports/R278-data/07-summary.json (26 cases x N=5); the driver is docs/reports/R282-data/scripts/time282.py, which calls baselines._b_tl_mlir.measure_case() directly. This entry's own gate verdict is: R282 G1 PASS 2/2 (max_rel 0.0 -- abs is exact). TO PUT IT IN THE POOL, adapters/handwritten.py would need a candidate that carries a device_us measured in another process; today _race() times every candidate itself in the caller's session (adapters/handwritten.py:215-247) and there is no channel for a pre-measured one. See R289.md divergence 1.

Handing _race a placeholder callable is not an alternative, and T289 measured what actually happens rather than predicting it: the D032 timer REFUSES a block that emits no device kernel (devicetimer.py:344, 'produced no device kernel'), and because _race puts every candidate in ONE session, that exception takes the whole selection session down -- the other candidates lose their measurement too. (R278 section 6.1 predicted a ~0 us candidate being elected as infinitely fast; the direction was right, the mechanism was not -- the timer's guard fires first. R289-data/02-counterfactual.json.) This baseline is measured out of process by baselines._b_tl_mlir.measure_case(); see docs/reports/R278.md. MEASURED ELSEWHERE, NOT MISSING: docs/reports/R282-data/22-timing-summary.json (34 cases x N=5 cross-process, D032 timer, bias band 3.2051%) and docs/reports/R278-data/07-summary.json (26 cases x N=5); the driver is docs/reports/R282-data/scripts/time282.py, which calls baselines._b_tl_mlir.measure_case() directly. This entry's own gate verdict is: R278 G1 PASS 1/5. TO PUT IT IN THE POOL, adapters/handwritten.py would need a candidate that carries a device_us measured in another process; today _race() times every candidate itself in the caller's session (adapters/handwritten.py:215-247) and there is no channel for a pre-measured one. See R289.md divergence 1.

property.name: baseline_refused
property.value: catlass-r252: 910B1 has no native FP8 Cube path, so only a soft-FP8 baseline could apply (ASCEND_910B1_HANDWRITTEN_BASELINES.md 4.C). CATLASS's 29_a2_fp8_e4m3_matmul IS that soft-FP8 kernel -- it declares ElementPrologueA=ElementPrologueB=int8_t converted by a prologue to half with ElementC=float, i.e. dequantize-to-fp16 then fp16 Cube -- but it is still not callable, for two of the three reasons R252 recorded: (a) R240 built it as an ELF executable (R240-data/build/examples/29_a2_fp8_e4m3_matmul/29_a2_fp8_e4m3_matmul), not a callable library, and it reads its operands from ./examples/29_a2_fp8_e4m3_matmul/input/a_8.bin rather than from caller pointers; (b) it takes NO scale tensor at all, while GemmFp8FwdOp's manifest asks for scale_mode=per_tensor and scale_mode=block128 -- so even with a wrapper the scaling semantics would not match, which is a ruling, not a wiring job. T351 UPDATE (2026-09-20): R252's third reason -- 'TileOPs registers NO Ascend builder for GemmFp8FwdOp / BmmFp8KNFwdOp / BmmFp8NKFwdOp' -- IS NO LONGER TRUE. All three now have builders in tileops/kernels/families/gemm.py (soft-FP8: bit-exact fp8->fp16 decode on the vector unit, fp16 Cube, fp32 accumulator), so there IS a tested side and a ratio does exist. What is measured against it is the D036 pool minus this entry: the vendor rung (a torch-eager composite that decodes the same bytes inside its own timing window) and torch.compile of that same composite, which D040 admits automatically. Reason (b) above is why nothing hand-written can join them. Recorded as public_handwritten_gap; see R252.md section 5 and R351.md section 5

property.name: baseline_refused
property.value: catlass-r252: 910B1 has no native FP8 Cube path, so only a soft-FP8 baseline could apply (ASCEND_910B1_HANDWRITTEN_BASELINES.md 4.C). CATLASS's 29_a2_fp8_e4m3_matmul IS that soft-FP8 kernel -- it declares ElementPrologueA=ElementPrologueB=int8_t converted by a prologue to half with ElementC=float, i.e. dequantize-to-fp16 then fp16 Cube -- but it is still not callable, for two of the three reasons R252 recorded: (a) R240 built it as an ELF executable (R240-data/build/examples/29_a2_fp8_e4m3_matmul/29_a2_fp8_e4m3_matmul), not a callable library, and it reads its operands from ./examples/29_a2_fp8_e4m3_matmul/input/a_8.bin rather than from caller pointers; (b) it takes NO scale tensor at all, while GemmFp8FwdOp's manifest asks for scale_mode=per_tensor and scale_mode=block128 -- so even with a wrapper the scaling semantics would not match, which is a ruling, not a wiring job. T351 UPDATE (2026-09-20): R252's third reason -- 'TileOPs registers NO Ascend builder for GemmFp8FwdOp / BmmFp8KNFwdOp / BmmFp8NKFwdOp' -- IS NO LONGER TRUE. All three now have builders in tileops/kernels/families/gemm.py (soft-FP8: bit-exact fp8->fp16 decode on the vector unit, fp16 Cube, fp32 accumulator), so there IS a tested side and a ratio does exist. What is measured against it is the D036 pool minus this entry: the vendor rung (a torch-eager composite that decodes the same bytes inside its own timing window) and torch.compile of that same composite, which D040 admits automatically. Reason (b) above is why nothing hand-written can join them. Recorded as public_handwritten_gap; see R252.md section 5 and R351.md section 5

property.value: tilelang-mlir-ascend: EluFwdOp/npuir_active (intent=unit_test, kernel=testing/npuir/active_ops/test_elu.py): tilelang-mlir-ascend cannot be raced in-process: its Python package is also called `tilelang` and its build/libtilelang.so shares our soname, so importing it here would either shadow or collide with the tilelang that compiled the tested side (D042/R272 -- STB_GNU_UNIQUE, and neither RTLD_LOCAL nor DEEPBIND gets out of it). Handing _race a placeholder callable is not an alternative, and T289 measured what actually happens rather than predicting it: the D032 timer REFUSES a block that emits no device kernel (devicetimer.py:344, 'produced no device kernel'), and because _race puts every candidate in ONE session, that exception takes the whole selection session down -- the other candidates lose their measurement too. (R278 section 6.1 predicted a ~0 us candidate being elected as infinitely fast; the direction was right, the mechanism was not -- the timer's guard fires first. R289-data/02-counterfactual.json.) This baseline is measured out of process by baselines._b_tl_mlir.measure_case(); see docs/reports/R278.md. MEASURED ELSEWHERE, NOT MISSING: docs/reports/R282-data/22-timing-summary.json (34 cases x N=5 cross-process, D032 timer, bias band 3.2051%) and docs/reports/R278-data/07-summary.json (26 cases x N=5); the driver is docs/reports/R282-data/scripts/time282.py, which calls baselines._b_tl_mlir.measure_case() directly. This entry's own gate verdict is: R282 G1 PASS 3/3. TO PUT IT IN THE POOL, adapters/handwritten.py would need a candidate that carries a device_us measured in another process; today _race() times every candidate itself in the caller's session (adapters/handwritten.py:215-247) and there is no channel for a pre-measured one. See R289.md divergence 1.

property.value: tilelang-mlir-ascend: EluFwdOp/npuir_active (intent=unit_test, kernel=testing/npuir/active_ops/test_elu.py): tilelang-mlir-ascend cannot be raced in-process: its Python package is also called `tilelang` and its build/libtilelang.so shares our soname, so importing it here would either shadow or collide with the tilelang that compiled the tested side (D042/R272 -- STB_GNU_UNIQUE, and neither RTLD_LOCAL nor DEEPBIND gets out of it). Handing _race a placeholder callable is not an alternative, and T289 measured what actually happens rather than predicting it: the D032 timer REFUSES a block that emits no device kernel (devicetimer.py:344, 'produced no device kernel'), and because _race puts every candidate in ONE session, that exception takes the whole selection session down -- the other candidates lose their measurement too. (R278 section 6.1 predicted a ~0 us candidate being elected as infinitely fast; the direction was right, the mechanism was not -- the timer's guard fires first. R289-data/02-counterfactual.json.) This baseline is measured out of process by baselines._b_tl_mlir.measure_case(); see docs/reports/R278.md. MEASURED ELSEWHERE, NOT MISSING: docs/reports/R282-data/22-timing-summary.json (34 cases x N=5 cross-process, D032 timer, bias band 3.2051%) and docs/reports/R278-data/07-summary.json (26 cases x N=5); the driver is docs/reports/R282-data/scripts/time282.py, which calls baselines._b_tl_mlir.measure_case() directly. This entry's own gate verdict is: R282 G1 PASS 3/3. TO PUT IT IN THE POOL, adapters/handwritten.py would need a candidate that carries a device_us measured in another process; today _race() times every candidate itself in the caller's session (adapters/handwritten.py:215-247) and there is no channel for a pre-measured one. See R289.md divergence 1.

property.name: baseline_refused
property.value: sgl-kernel-npu: torch.ops.npu.lightning_indexer requires exactly 64 query heads per KV group -- measured error at the manifest shape: 'lightning_indexer: N1 is 32, N2 is 1, N1 divided by N2 must equal 64.' This case has heads=0 / kv_group=1 = 0. Two further mismatches make it the wrong boundary even at 64 heads: it FUSES the selection (it returns int32 indices of shape [.., sparse_count], while FP8LightningIndexerFwdOp returns the logits [B, S, Skv, G] and TopkSelectorFwdOp does the selection as a separate operator -- so SGL's one kernel spans TWO of ours and never writes the logits to HBM), and its key must be a paged PA_BSND cache with a block_table, while our index_k is a plain [B, Skv, G, D] tensor. The fp8 manifest cases fail earlier still: torch_npu cannot even copy into float8_e4m3fn on this build (aclnnInplaceCopy -> 561103). coverage_status = public_handwritten_gap

property.name: baseline_refused
property.value: ops-nn-gemm: FP8QuantFwdOp quantizes to float8_e4m3fn with a per-(b,s,g)-row absmax scale (amax/448). The closest ops-nn kernel is quant/dynamic_quant via aclnnDynamicQuant, which R252 measured to be exactly the same algorithm with an INT8 destination (measured scale/(amax/127) == 1.000000 for fp16 and bf16), and the entry point takes no dstType argument. int8-vs-e4m3 is a dtype mismatch under ASCEND_910B1_HANDWRITTEN_BASELINES.md 5.6, so nothing hand-written can join the pool. R355 UPDATE: the second half of this reason -- 'TileOPs also registers no Ascend builder for FP8QuantFwdOp (its forward raises on a non-CUDA tensor), so there is no tested side either' -- IS NO LONGER TRUE, and neither half of it ever was: R331 showed the forward has no CUDA guard at all (it checks device.type != 'npu'), and R355 registered the builder in tileops/kernels/families/gemm.py's sibling tileops/kernels/families/two_pass.py (build_fp8_quant), so there IS a tested side and a ratio does exist. What it is measured against is the D036 pool minus this entry: a torch-eager composite that does the absmax, the scale and the e4m3 encode inside its own timing window, because no aclnn operator on 910B produces float8_e4m3fn at all (npu_quantize rejects e4m3 with 161002). Still recorded as public_handwritten_gap; see R252.md section 4 and R355.md section 5

property.name: baseline_refused
property.value: catlass-r252: 910B1 has no native FP8 Cube path, so only a soft-FP8 baseline could apply (ASCEND_910B1_HANDWRITTEN_BASELINES.md 4.C). CATLASS's 29_a2_fp8_e4m3_matmul IS that soft-FP8 kernel -- it declares ElementPrologueA=ElementPrologueB=int8_t converted by a prologue to half with ElementC=float, i.e. dequantize-to-fp16 then fp16 Cube -- but it is still not callable, for two of the three reasons R252 recorded: (a) R240 built it as an ELF executable (R240-data/build/examples/29_a2_fp8_e4m3_matmul/29_a2_fp8_e4m3_matmul), not a callable library, and it reads its operands from ./examples/29_a2_fp8_e4m3_matmul/input/a_8.bin rather than from caller pointers; (b) it takes NO scale tensor at all, while GemmFp8FwdOp's manifest asks for scale_mode=per_tensor and scale_mode=block128 -- so even with a wrapper the scaling semantics would not match, which is a ruling, not a wiring job. T351 UPDATE (2026-09-20): R252's third reason -- 'TileOPs registers NO Ascend builder for GemmFp8FwdOp / BmmFp8KNFwdOp / BmmFp8NKFwdOp' -- IS NO LONGER TRUE. All three now have builders in tileops/kernels/families/gemm.py (soft-FP8: bit-exact fp8->fp16 decode on the vector unit, fp16 Cube, fp32 accumulator), so there IS a tested side and a ratio does exist. What is measured against it is the D036 pool minus this entry: the vendor rung (a torch-eager composite that decodes the same bytes inside its own timing window) and torch.compile of that same composite, which D040 admits automatically. Reason (b) above is why nothing hand-written can join them. Recorded as public_handwritten_gap; see R252.md section 5 and R351.md section 5

property.name: baseline_refused
property.value: catlass-r252: 910B1 has no native FP8 Cube path, so only a soft-FP8 baseline could apply (ASCEND_910B1_HANDWRITTEN_BASELINES.md 4.C). CATLASS's 29_a2_fp8_e4m3_matmul IS that soft-FP8 kernel -- it declares ElementPrologueA=ElementPrologueB=int8_t converted by a prologue to half with ElementC=float, i.e. dequantize-to-fp16 then fp16 Cube -- but it is still not callable, for two of the three reasons R252 recorded: (a) R240 built it as an ELF executable (R240-data/build/examples/29_a2_fp8_e4m3_matmul/29_a2_fp8_e4m3_matmul), not a callable library, and it reads its operands from ./examples/29_a2_fp8_e4m3_matmul/input/a_8.bin rather than from caller pointers; (b) it takes NO scale tensor at all, while GemmFp8FwdOp's manifest asks for scale_mode=per_tensor and scale_mode=block128 -- so even with a wrapper the scaling semantics would not match, which is a ruling, not a wiring job. T351 UPDATE (2026-09-20): R252's third reason -- 'TileOPs registers NO Ascend builder for GemmFp8FwdOp / BmmFp8KNFwdOp / BmmFp8NKFwdOp' -- IS NO LONGER TRUE. All three now have builders in tileops/kernels/families/gemm.py (soft-FP8: bit-exact fp8->fp16 decode on the vector unit, fp16 Cube, fp32 accumulator), so there IS a tested side and a ratio does exist. What is measured against it is the D036 pool minus this entry: the vendor rung (a torch-eager composite that decodes the same bytes inside its own timing window) and torch.compile of that same composite, which D040 admits automatically. Reason (b) above is why nothing hand-written can join them. Recorded as public_handwritten_gap; see R252.md section 5 and R351.md section 5

property.name: baseline_refused
property.value: catlass-r252: 910B1 has no native FP8 Cube path, so only a soft-FP8 baseline could apply (ASCEND_910B1_HANDWRITTEN_BASELINES.md 4.C). CATLASS's 29_a2_fp8_e4m3_matmul IS that soft-FP8 kernel -- it declares ElementPrologueA=ElementPrologueB=int8_t converted by a prologue to half with ElementC=float, i.e. dequantize-to-fp16 then fp16 Cube -- but it is still not callable, for two of the three reasons R252 recorded: (a) R240 built it as an ELF executable (R240-data/build/examples/29_a2_fp8_e4m3_matmul/29_a2_fp8_e4m3_matmul), not a callable library, and it reads its operands from ./examples/29_a2_fp8_e4m3_matmul/input/a_8.bin rather than from caller pointers; (b) it takes NO scale tensor at all, while GemmFp8FwdOp's manifest asks for scale_mode=per_tensor and scale_mode=block128 -- so even with a wrapper the scaling semantics would not match, which is a ruling, not a wiring job. T351 UPDATE (2026-09-20): R252's third reason -- 'TileOPs registers NO Ascend builder for GemmFp8FwdOp / BmmFp8KNFwdOp / BmmFp8NKFwdOp' -- IS NO LONGER TRUE. All three now have builders in tileops/kernels/families/gemm.py (soft-FP8: bit-exact fp8->fp16 decode on the vector unit, fp16 Cube, fp32 accumulator), so there IS a tested side and a ratio does exist. What is measured against it is the D036 pool minus this entry: the vendor rung (a torch-eager composite that decodes the same bytes inside its own timing window) and torch.compile of that same composite, which D040 admits automatically. Reason (b) above is why nothing hand-written can join them. Recorded as public_handwritten_gap; see R252.md section 5 and R351.md section 5

property.name: baseline_refused
property.value: catlass-r252: 910B1 has no native FP8 Cube path, so only a soft-FP8 baseline could apply (ASCEND_910B1_HANDWRITTEN_BASELINES.md 4.C). CATLASS's 29_a2_fp8_e4m3_matmul IS that soft-FP8 kernel -- it declares ElementPrologueA=ElementPrologueB=int8_t converted by a prologue to half with ElementC=float, i.e. dequantize-to-fp16 then fp16 Cube -- but it is still not callable, for two of the three reasons R252 recorded: (a) R240 built it as an ELF executable (R240-data/build/examples/29_a2_fp8_e4m3_matmul/29_a2_fp8_e4m3_matmul), not a callable library, and it reads its operands from ./examples/29_a2_fp8_e4m3_matmul/input/a_8.bin rather than from caller pointers; (b) it takes NO scale tensor at all, while GemmFp8FwdOp's manifest asks for scale_mode=per_tensor and scale_mode=block128 -- so even with a wrapper the scaling semantics would not match, which is a ruling, not a wiring job. T351 UPDATE (2026-09-20): R252's third reason -- 'TileOPs registers NO Ascend builder for GemmFp8FwdOp / BmmFp8KNFwdOp / BmmFp8NKFwdOp' -- IS NO LONGER TRUE. All three now have builders in tileops/kernels/families/gemm.py (soft-FP8: bit-exact fp8->fp16 decode on the vector unit, fp16 Cube, fp32 accumulator), so there IS a tested side and a ratio does exist. What is measured against it is the D036 pool minus this entry: the vendor rung (a torch-eager composite that decodes the same bytes inside its own timing window) and torch.compile of that same composite, which D040 admits automatically. Reason (b) above is why nothing hand-written can join them. Recorded as public_handwritten_gap; see R252.md section 5 and R351.md section 5

property.name: baseline_refused
property.value: catlass-r252: 910B1 has no native FP8 Cube path, so only a soft-FP8 baseline could apply (ASCEND_910B1_HANDWRITTEN_BASELINES.md 4.C). CATLASS's 29_a2_fp8_e4m3_matmul IS that soft-FP8 kernel -- it declares ElementPrologueA=ElementPrologueB=int8_t converted by a prologue to half with ElementC=float, i.e. dequantize-to-fp16 then fp16 Cube -- but it is still not callable, for two of the three reasons R252 recorded: (a) R240 built it as an ELF executable (R240-data/build/examples/29_a2_fp8_e4m3_matmul/29_a2_fp8_e4m3_matmul), not a callable library, and it reads its operands from ./examples/29_a2_fp8_e4m3_matmul/input/a_8.bin rather than from caller pointers; (b) it takes NO scale tensor at all, while GemmFp8FwdOp's manifest asks for scale_mode=per_tensor and scale_mode=block128 -- so even with a wrapper the scaling semantics would not match, which is a ruling, not a wiring job. T351 UPDATE (2026-09-20): R252's third reason -- 'TileOPs registers NO Ascend builder for GemmFp8FwdOp / BmmFp8KNFwdOp / BmmFp8NKFwdOp' -- IS NO LONGER TRUE. All three now have builders in tileops/kernels/families/gemm.py (soft-FP8: bit-exact fp8->fp16 decode on the vector unit, fp16 Cube, fp32 accumulator), so there IS a tested side and a ratio does exist. What is measured against it is the D036 pool minus this entry: the vendor rung (a torch-eager composite that decodes the same bytes inside its own timing window) and torch.compile of that same composite, which D040 admits automatically. Reason (b) above is why nothing hand-written can join them. Recorded as public_handwritten_gap; see R252.md section 5 and R351.md section 5

property.name: baseline_refused
property.value: tilelang-ascend: trans_b=False is served by examples/gemm/example_gemm_intrinsic.py (B is (K, N)); this entry is the NT example, B is (N, K); tilelang-mlir-ascend: GemmFwdOp/example_gemm (intent=example, kernel=examples/gemm/example_gemm.py): tilelang-mlir-ascend cannot be raced in-process: its Python package is also called `tilelang` and its build/libtilelang.so shares our soname, so importing it here would either shadow or collide with the tilelang that compiled the tested side (D042/R272 -- STB_GNU_UNIQUE, and neither RTLD_LOCAL nor DEEPBIND gets out of it). Handing _race a placeholder callable is not an alternative, and T289 measured what actually happens rather than predicting it: the D032 timer REFUSES a block that emits no device kernel (devicetimer.py:344, 'produced no device kernel'), and because _race puts every candidate in ONE session, that exception takes the whole selection session down -- the other candidates lose their measurement too. (R278 section 6.1 predicted a ~0 us candidate being elected as infinitely fast; the direction was right, the mechanism was not -- the timer's guard fires first. R289-data/02-counterfactual.json.) This baseline is measured out of process by baselines._b_tl_mlir.measure_case(); see docs/reports/R278.md. MEASURED ELSEWHERE, NOT MISSING: docs/reports/R282-data/22-timing-summary.json (34 cases x N=5 cross-process, D032 timer, bias band 3.2051%) and docs/reports/R278-data/07-summary.json (26 cases x N=5); the driver is docs/reports/R282-data/scripts/time282.py, which calls baselines._b_tl_mlir.measure_case() directly. This entry's own gate verdict is: R278 G1 PASS 2/2 (the one NN case; 11 trans_b cases refused). TO PUT IT IN THE POOL, adapters/handwritten.py would need a candidate that carries a device_us measured in another process; today _race() times every candidate itself in the caller's session (adapters/handwritten.py:215-247) and there is no channel for a pre-measured one. See R289.md divergence 1.

(R278 section 6.1 predicted a ~0 us candidate being elected as infinitely fast; the direction was right, the mechanism was not -- the timer's guard fires first. R289-data/02-counterfactual.json.) This baseline is measured out of process by baselines._b_tl_mlir.measure_case(); see docs/reports/R278.md. property.name: baseline_refused
property.value: catlass: libcatlass_gemm_capi.so instantiates BasicMatmul for half only (ElementA=ElementB=ElementC=half in catlass_gemm_capi.cpp); bf16 needs a second template instantiation, which this round did not add; tilelang-ascend: trans_b=True is served by examples/gemm/example_gemm_transpose_l1.py (B stored (N, K)); this entry is the NN example, B is (K, N); tilelang-mlir-ascend: GemmFwdOp/example_gemm (intent=example, kernel=examples/gemm/example_gemm.py): tilelang-mlir-ascend cannot be raced in-process: its Python package is also called `tilelang` and its build/libtilelang.so shares our soname, so importing it here would either shadow or collide with the tilelang that compiled the tested side (D042/R272 -- STB_GNU_UNIQUE, and neither RTLD_LOCAL nor DEEPBIND gets out of it). Handing _race a placeholder callable is not an alternative, and T289 measured what actually happens rather than predicting it: the D032 timer REFUSES a block that emits no device kernel (devicetimer.py:344, 'produced no device kernel'), and because _race puts every candidate in ONE session, that exception takes the whole selection session down -- the other candidates lose their measurement too. (R278 section 6.1 predicted a ~0 us candidate being elected as infinitely fast; the direction was right, the mechanism was not -- the timer's guard fires first. R289-data/02-counterfactual.json.) This baseline is measured out of process by baselines._b_tl_mlir.measure_case(); see docs/reports/R278.md. MEASURED ELSEWHERE, NOT MISSING: docs/reports/R282-data/22-timing-summary.json (34 cases x N=5 cross-process, D032 timer, bias band 3.2051%) and docs/reports/R278-data/07-summary.json (26 cases x N=5); the driver is docs/reports/R282-data/scripts/time282.py, which calls baselines._b_tl_mlir.measure_case() directly. This entry's own gate verdict is: R278 G1 PASS 2/2 (the one NN case; 11 trans_b cases refused). TO PUT IT IN THE POOL, adapters/handwritten.py would need a candidate that carries a device_us measured in another process; today _race() times every candidate itself in the caller's session (adapters/handwritten.py:215-247) and there is no channel for a pre-measured one. See R289.md divergence 1.

property.value: catlass: libcatlass_gemm_capi.so instantiates LayoutA=LayoutB=RowMajor only; trans_a/trans_b need a ColumnMajor instantiation, which this round did not add; tilelang-ascend: trans_b=True is served by examples/gemm/example_gemm_transpose_l1.py (B stored (N, K)); this entry is the NN example, B is (K, N); tilelang-mlir-ascend: GemmFwdOp/example_gemm (intent=example, kernel=examples/gemm/example_gemm.py): tilelang-mlir-ascend cannot be raced in-process: its Python package is also called `tilelang` and its build/libtilelang.so shares our soname, so importing it here would either shadow or collide with the tilelang that compiled the tested side (D042/R272 -- STB_GNU_UNIQUE, and neither RTLD_LOCAL nor DEEPBIND gets out of it). Handing _race a placeholder callable is not an alternative, and T289 measured what actually happens rather than predicting it: the D032 timer REFUSES a block that emits no device kernel (devicetimer.py:344, 'produced no device kernel'), and because _race puts every candidate in ONE session, that exception takes the whole selection session down -- the other candidates lose their measurement too. (R278 section 6.1 predicted a ~0 us candidate being elected as infinitely fast; the direction was right, the mechanism was not -- the timer's guard fires first. R289-data/02-counterfactual.json.) This baseline is measured out of process by baselines._b_tl_mlir.measure_case(); see docs/reports/R278.md. MEASURED ELSEWHERE, NOT MISSING: docs/reports/R282-data/22-timing-summary.json (34 cases x N=5 cross-process, D032 timer, bias band 3.2051%) and docs/reports/R278-data/07-summary.json (26 cases x N=5); the driver is docs/reports/R282-data/scripts/time282.py, which calls baselines._b_tl_mlir.measure_case() directly. This entry's own gate verdict is: R278 G1 PASS 2/2 (the one NN case; 11 trans_b cases refused). TO PUT IT IN THE POOL, adapters/handwritten.py would need a candidate that carries a device_us measured in another process; today _race() times every candidate itself in the caller's session (adapters/handwritten.py:215-247) and there is no channel for a pre-measured one. See R289.md divergence 1.

(R278 section 6.1 predicted a ~0 us candidate being elected as infinitely fast; the direction was right, the mechanism was not -- the timer's guard fires first. R289-data/02-counterfactual.json.) This entry's own gate verdict is: R278 G1 PASS 2/2 (the one NN case; 11 trans_b cases refused). TO PUT IT IN THE POOL, adapters/handwritten.py would need a candidate that carries a device_us measured in another process; today _race() times every candidate itself in the caller's session (adapters/handwritten.py:215-247) and there is no channel for a pre-measured one. See R289.md divergence 1.

Handing _race a placeholder callable is not an alternative, and T289 measured what actually happens rather than predicting it: the D032 timer REFUSES a block that emits no device kernel (devicetimer.py:344, 'produced no device kernel'), and because _race puts every candidate in ONE session, that exception takes the whole selection session down -- the other candidates lose their measurement too. (R278 section 6.1 predicted a ~0 us candidate being elected as infinitely fast; the direction was right, the mechanism was not -- the timer's guard fires first. R289-data/02-counterfactual.json.) This baseline is measured out of process by baselines._b_tl_mlir.measure_case(); see docs/reports/R278.md. MEASURED ELSEWHERE, NOT MISSING: docs/reports/R282-data/22-timing-summary.json (34 cases x N=5 cross-process, D032 timer, bias band 3.2051%) and docs/reports/R278-data/07-summary.json (26 cases x N=5); the driver is docs/reports/R282-data/scripts/time282.py, which calls baselines._b_tl_mlir.measure_case() directly. This entry's own gate verdict is: R278 G1 PASS 2/2 (the one NN case; 11 trans_b cases refused). TO PUT IT IN THE POOL, adapters/handwritten.py would need a candidate that carries a device_us measured in another process; today _race() times every candidate itself in the caller's session (adapters/handwritten.py:215-247) and there is no channel for a pre-measured one. See R289.md divergence 1.

Handing _race a placeholder callable is not an alternative, and T289 measured what actually happens rather than predicting it: the D032 timer REFUSES a block that emits no device kernel (devicetimer.py:344, 'produced no device kernel'), and because _race puts every candidate in ONE session, that exception takes the whole selection session down -- the other candidates lose their measurement too. (R278 section 6.1 predicted a ~0 us candidate being elected as infinitely fast; the direction was right, the mechanism was not -- the timer's guard fires first. R289-data/02-counterfactual.json.) This baseline is measured out of process by baselines._b_tl_mlir.measure_case(); see docs/reports/R278.md. This entry's own gate verdict is: R278 G1 PASS 2/2 (the one NN case; 11 trans_b cases refused). TO PUT IT IN THE POOL, adapters/handwritten.py would need a candidate that carries a device_us measured in another process; today _race() times every candidate itself in the caller's session (adapters/handwritten.py:215-247) and there is no channel for a pre-measured one. Handing _race a placeholder callable is not an alternative, and T289 measured what actually happens rather than predicting it: the D032 timer REFUSES a block that emits no device kernel (devicetimer.py:344, 'produced no device kernel'), and because _race puts every candidate in ONE session, that exception takes the whole selection session down -- the other candidates lose their measurement too. (R278 section 6.1 predicted a ~0 us candidate being elected as infinitely fast; the direction was right, the mechanism was not -- the timer's guard fires first. R289-data/02-counterfactual.json.) This baseline is measured out of process by baselines._b_tl_mlir.measure_case(); see docs/reports/R278.md. MEASURED ELSEWHERE, NOT MISSING: docs/reports/R282-data/22-timing-summary.json (34 cases x N=5 cross-process, D032 timer, bias band 3.2051%) and docs/reports/R278-data/07-summary.json (26 cases x N=5); the driver is docs/reports/R282-data/scripts/time282.py, which calls baselines._b_tl_mlir.measure_case() directly. This entry's own gate verdict is: R278 G1 PASS 2/2 (the one NN case; 11 trans_b cases refused). TO PUT IT IN THE POOL, adapters/handwritten.py would need a candidate that carries a device_us measured in another process; today _race() times every candidate itself in the caller's session (adapters/handwritten.py:215-247) and there is no channel for a pre-measured one. See R289.md divergence 1.

Handing _race a placeholder callable is not an alternative, and T289 measured what actually happens rather than predicting it: the D032 timer REFUSES a block that emits no device kernel (devicetimer.py:344, 'produced no device kernel'), and because _race puts every candidate in ONE session, that exception takes the whole selection session down -- the other candidates lose their measurement too. (R278 section 6.1 predicted a ~0 us candidate being elected as infinitely fast; the direction was right, the mechanism was not -- the timer's guard fires first. R289-data/02-counterfactual.json.) This baseline is measured out of process by baselines._b_tl_mlir.measure_case(); see docs/reports/R278.md. MEASURED ELSEWHERE, NOT MISSING: docs/reports/R282-data/22-timing-summary.json (34 cases x N=5 cross-process, D032 timer, bias band 3.2051%) and docs/reports/R278-data/07-summary.json (26 cases x N=5); the driver is docs/reports/R282-data/scripts/time282.py, which calls baselines._b_tl_mlir.measure_case() directly. This entry's own gate verdict is: 🚨 R282 G1 FAIL 0/2 -- max_abs 0.00390625 vs atol=1e-3, guards clean: 2 float16 ulps from a different rounding order. A numerical-contract miss, NOT a defect. TO PUT IT IN THE POOL, adapters/handwritten.py would need a candidate that carries a device_us measured in another process; today _race() times every candidate itself in the caller's session (adapters/handwritten.py:215-247) and there is no channel for a pre-measured one. See R289.md divergence 1.

property.name: baseline_refused
property.value: ops-nn: ops-nn's aclnnLayerNorm dispatches to the compiled LayerNormV4 kernel only for bfloat16 with a reduce axis of 1024 or 4096 on ascend910b (IsV4SocCheck in norm/layer_norm_v4/op_host/op_api/aclnn_layer_norm.cpp); for float16/D=4096 it runs CANN's built-in LayerNormV3, which this package does not contain (strace: R251-data/logs/tier-check-layernorm-shapes.log). Reporting that as a handwritten baseline would be the PROJECT_STATE 13.90 fallback; tilelang-mlir-ascend: LayerNormFwdOp/high_perf (intent=example, kernel=examples/norm/layer_norm.py): tilelang-mlir-ascend cannot be raced in-process: its Python package is also called `tilelang` and its build/libtilelang.so shares our soname, so importing it here would either shadow or collide with the tilelang that compiled the tested side (D042/R272 -- STB_GNU_UNIQUE, and neither RTLD_LOCAL nor DEEPBIND gets out of it). Handing _race a placeholder callable is not an alternative, and T289 measured what actually happens rather than predicting it: the D032 timer REFUSES a block that emits no device kernel (devicetimer.py:344, 'produced no device kernel'), and because _race puts every candidate in ONE session, that exception takes the whole selection session down -- the other candidates lose their measurement too. Handing _race a placeholder callable is not an alternative, and T289 measured what actually happens rather than predicting it: the D032 timer REFUSES a block that emits no device kernel (devicetimer.py:344, 'produced no device kernel'), and because _race puts every candidate in ONE session, that exception takes the whole selection session down -- the other candidates lose their measurement too. This baseline is measured out of process by baselines._b_tl_mlir.measure_case(); see docs/reports/R278.md. Handing _race a placeholder callable is not an alternative, and T289 measured what actually happens rather than predicting it: the D032 timer REFUSES a block that emits no device kernel (devicetimer.py:344, 'produced no device kernel'), and because _race puts every candidate in ONE session, that exception takes the whole selection session down -- the other candidates lose their measurement too. (R278 section 6.1 predicted a ~0 us candidate being elected as infinitely fast; the direction was right, the mechanism was not -- the timer's guard fires first. R289-data/02-counterfactual.json.) This baseline is measured out of process by baselines._b_tl_mlir.measure_case(); see docs/reports/R278.md. This entry's own gate verdict is: R282 G1 PASS 2/2. TO PUT IT IN THE POOL, adapters/handwritten.py would need a candidate that carries a device_us measured in another process; today _race() times every candidate itself in the caller's session (adapters/handwritten.py:215-247) and there is no channel for a pre-measured one. property.name: baseline_refused
property.value: tilelang-ascend: leaky_relu's negative slope is the literal 2.0 in the kernel body (T.tile.leaky_relu(b_ub, a_ub, 2.0); the factory takes no slope argument), while our golden is negative_slope=0.01 -- a different function, not a different shape (G2/G4); tilelang-mlir-ascend: LeakyReluFwdOp/npuir_active (intent=unit_test, kernel=testing/npuir/active_ops/test_leaky_relu.py): tilelang-mlir-ascend cannot be raced in-process: its Python package is also called `tilelang` and its build/libtilelang.so shares our soname, so importing it here would either shadow or collide with the tilelang that compiled the tested side (D042/R272 -- STB_GNU_UNIQUE, and neither RTLD_LOCAL nor DEEPBIND gets out of it). Handing _race a placeholder callable is not an alternative, and T289 measured what actually happens rather than predicting it: the D032 timer REFUSES a block that emits no device kernel (devicetimer.py:344, 'produced no device kernel'), and because _race puts every candidate in ONE session, that exception takes the whole selection session down -- the other candidates lose their measurement too. (R278 section 6.1 predicted a ~0 us candidate being elected as infinitely fast; the direction was right, the mechanism was not -- the timer's guard fires first. R289-data/02-counterfactual.json.) This baseline is measured out of process by baselines._b_tl_mlir.measure_case(); see docs/reports/R278.md. MEASURED ELSEWHERE, NOT MISSING: docs/reports/R282-data/22-timing-summary.json (34 cases x N=5 cross-process, D032 timer, bias band 3.2051%) and docs/reports/R278-data/07-summary.json (26 cases x N=5); the driver is docs/reports/R282-data/scripts/time282.py, which calls baselines._b_tl_mlir.measure_case() directly. This entry's own gate verdict is: R282 G1 PASS 2/2. TO PUT IT IN THE POOL, adapters/handwritten.py would need a candidate that carries a device_us measured in another process; today _race() times every candidate itself in the caller's session (adapters/handwritten.py:215-247) and there is no channel for a pre-measured one. See R289.md divergence 1.

property.value: tilelang-ascend: leaky_relu's negative slope is the literal 2.0 in the kernel body (T.tile.leaky_relu(b_ub, a_ub, 2.0); the factory takes no slope argument), while our golden is negative_slope=0.01 -- a different function, not a different shape (G2/G4); tilelang-mlir-ascend: LeakyReluFwdOp/npuir_active (intent=unit_test, kernel=testing/npuir/active_ops/test_leaky_relu.py): tilelang-mlir-ascend cannot be raced in-process: its Python package is also called `tilelang` and its build/libtilelang.so shares our soname, so importing it here would either shadow or collide with the tilelang that compiled the tested side (D042/R272 -- STB_GNU_UNIQUE, and neither RTLD_LOCAL nor DEEPBIND gets out of it). Handing _race a placeholder callable is not an alternative, and T289 measured what actually happens rather than predicting it: the D032 timer REFUSES a block that emits no device kernel (devicetimer.py:344, 'produced no device kernel'), and because _race puts every candidate in ONE session, that exception takes the whole selection session down -- the other candidates lose their measurement too. (R278 section 6.1 predicted a ~0 us candidate being elected as infinitely fast; the direction was right, the mechanism was not -- the timer's guard fires first. R289-data/02-counterfactual.json.) This baseline is measured out of process by baselines._b_tl_mlir.measure_case(); see docs/reports/R278.md. MEASURED ELSEWHERE, NOT MISSING: docs/reports/R282-data/22-timing-summary.json (34 cases x N=5 cross-process, D032 timer, bias band 3.2051%) and docs/reports/R278-data/07-summary.json (26 cases x N=5); the driver is docs/reports/R282-data/scripts/time282.py, which calls baselines._b_tl_mlir.measure_case() directly. This entry's own gate verdict is: R282 G1 PASS 2/2. TO PUT IT IN THE POOL, adapters/handwritten.py would need a candidate that carries a device_us measured in another process; today _race() times every candidate itself in the caller's session (adapters/handwritten.py:215-247) and there is no channel for a pre-measured one. See R289.md divergence 1.

property.value: tilelang-mlir-ascend: Log2FwdOp/example (intent=example, kernel=examples/elementwise/example_elementwise_log2.py): tilelang-mlir-ascend cannot be raced in-process: its Python package is also called `tilelang` and its build/libtilelang.so shares our soname, so importing it here would either shadow or collide with the tilelang that compiled the tested side (D042/R272 -- STB_GNU_UNIQUE, and neither RTLD_LOCAL nor DEEPBIND gets out of it). Handing _race a placeholder callable is not an alternative, and T289 measured what actually happens rather than predicting it: the D032 timer REFUSES a block that emits no device kernel (devicetimer.py:344, 'produced no device kernel'), and because _race puts every candidate in ONE session, that exception takes the whole selection session down -- the other candidates lose their measurement too. (R278 section 6.1 predicted a ~0 us candidate being elected as infinitely fast; the direction was right, the mechanism was not -- the timer's guard fires first. R289-data/02-counterfactual.json.) This baseline is measured out of process by baselines._b_tl_mlir.measure_case(); see docs/reports/R278.md. MEASURED ELSEWHERE, NOT MISSING: docs/reports/R282-data/22-timing-summary.json (34 cases x N=5 cross-process, D032 timer, bias band 3.2051%) and docs/reports/R278-data/07-summary.json (26 cases x N=5); the driver is docs/reports/R282-data/scripts/time282.py, which calls baselines._b_tl_mlir.measure_case() directly. This entry's own gate verdict is: 🚨 R282 G1 FAIL 0/4 -- max_abs 4.32 (the full output range) and a non-zero R240 restore guard. Correct ONLY at its own 16x16 test shape, wrong at every larger shape INCLUDING at their published 8x8 tile. See R282-data/04-ub-family-probe.txt. TO PUT IT IN THE POOL, adapters/handwritten.py would need a candidate that carries a device_us measured in another process; today _race() times every candidate itself in the caller's session (adapters/handwritten.py:215-247) and there is no channel for a pre-measured one. See R289.md divergence 1.

property.name: baseline_refused
property.value: tilelang-mlir-ascend: RMSNormFwdOp/high_perf (intent=example, kernel=examples/norm/rms_norm.py): tilelang-mlir-ascend cannot be raced in-process: its Python package is also called `tilelang` and its build/libtilelang.so shares our soname, so importing it here would either shadow or collide with the tilelang that compiled the tested side (D042/R272 -- STB_GNU_UNIQUE, and neither RTLD_LOCAL nor DEEPBIND gets out of it). Handing _race a placeholder callable is not an alternative, and T289 measured what actually happens rather than predicting it: the D032 timer REFUSES a block that emits no device kernel (devicetimer.py:344, 'produced no device kernel'), and because _race puts every candidate in ONE session, that exception takes the whole selection session down -- the other candidates lose their measurement too. (R278 section 6.1 predicted a ~0 us candidate being elected as infinitely fast; the direction was right, the mechanism was not -- the timer's guard fires first. R289-data/02-counterfactual.json.) This baseline is measured out of process by baselines._b_tl_mlir.measure_case(); see docs/reports/R278.md. MEASURED ELSEWHERE, NOT MISSING: docs/reports/R282-data/22-timing-summary.json (34 cases x N=5 cross-process, D032 timer, bias band 3.2051%) and docs/reports/R278-data/07-summary.json (26 cases x N=5); the driver is docs/reports/R282-data/scripts/time282.py, which calls baselines._b_tl_mlir.measure_case() directly. This entry's own gate verdict is: 🚨 R278 G1 FAIL 0/2 -- accumulates into an un-cleared fragment; R240 restore guard 0.203 where it must be 0 (R278 section 4.2). property.value: tilelang-ascend: no legal block_M for extent 1: the example needs block_M to divide it exactly and be a multiple of 2 (published value 128); tilelang-mlir-ascend: ReluFwdOp/unittest_vec (intent=unit_test, kernel=unittest/npuir/test_vec_relu_2d.py): tilelang-mlir-ascend cannot be raced in-process: its Python package is also called `tilelang` and its build/libtilelang.so shares our soname, so importing it here would either shadow or collide with the tilelang that compiled the tested side (D042/R272 -- STB_GNU_UNIQUE, and neither RTLD_LOCAL nor DEEPBIND gets out of it). Handing _race a placeholder callable is not an alternative, and T289 measured what actually happens rather than predicting it: the D032 timer REFUSES a block that emits no device kernel (devicetimer.py:344, 'produced no device kernel'), and because _race puts every candidate in ONE session, that exception takes the whole selection session down -- the other candidates lose their measurement too. (R278 section 6.1 predicted a ~0 us candidate being elected as infinitely fast; the direction was right, the mechanism was not -- the timer's guard fires first. R289-data/02-counterfactual.json.) This baseline is measured out of process by baselines._b_tl_mlir.measure_case(); see docs/reports/R278.md. MEASURED ELSEWHERE, NOT MISSING: docs/reports/R282-data/22-timing-summary.json (34 cases x N=5 cross-process, D032 timer, bias band 3.2051%) and docs/reports/R278-data/07-summary.json (26 cases x N=5); the driver is docs/reports/R282-data/scripts/time282.py, which calls baselines._b_tl_mlir.measure_case() directly. This entry's own gate verdict is: 🚨 R282 G1 FAIL 0/2 -- max_abs 4.96 and R240 restore guard 4.98 (must be 0). Bit-identical under Developer and Expert, so it is not the mode. The sibling in active_ops computes the same operator correctly on the same tensors, which is the control. TO PUT IT IN THE POOL, adapters/handwritten.py would need a candidate that carries a device_us measured in another process; today _race() times every candidate itself in the caller's session (adapters/handwritten.py:215-247) and there is no channel for a pre-measured one. See R289.md divergence 1.; tilelang-mlir-ascend: ReluFwdOp/npuir_active (intent=unit_test, kernel=testing/npuir/active_ops/test_relu.py): tilelang-mlir-ascend cannot be raced in-process: its Python package is also called `tilelang` and its build/libtilelang.so shares our soname, so importing it here would either shadow or collide with the tilelang that compiled the tested side (D042/R272 -- STB_GNU_UNIQUE, and neither RTLD_LOCAL nor DEEPBIND gets out of it). Handing _race a placeholder callable is not an alternative, and T289 measured what actually happens rather than predicting it: the D032 timer REFUSES a block that emits no device kernel (devicetimer.py:344, 'produced no device kernel'), and because _race puts every candidate in ONE session, that exception takes the whole selection session down -- the other candidates lose their measurement too. (R278 section 6.1 predicted a ~0 us candidate being elected as infinitely fast; the direction was right, the mechanism was not -- the timer's guard fires first. R289-data/02-counterfactual.json.) This baseline is measured out of process by baselines._b_tl_mlir.measure_case(); see docs/reports/R278.md. MEASURED ELSEWHERE, NOT MISSING: docs/reports/R282-data/22-timing-summary.json (34 cases x N=5 cross-process, D032 timer, bias band 3.2051%) and docs/reports/R278-data/07-summary.json (26 cases x N=5); the driver is docs/reports/R282-data/scripts/time282.py, which calls baselines._b_tl_mlir.measure_case() directly. This entry's own gate verdict is: R282 G1 PASS 3/3 (fp16 + bf16 + the (1,4096) row). TO PUT IT IN THE POOL, adapters/handwritten.py would need a candidate that carries a device_us measured in another process; today _race() times every candidate itself in the caller's session (adapters/handwritten.py:215-247) and there is no channel for a pre-measured one. property.value: tilelang-mlir-ascend: RopeLlama31FwdOp/rope_llama31 (intent=example, kernel=examples/posembedding/rope_llama31/rope_llama31.py): tilelang-mlir-ascend cannot be raced in-process: its Python package is also called `tilelang` and its build/libtilelang.so shares our soname, so importing it here would either shadow or collide with the tilelang that compiled the tested side (D042/R272 -- STB_GNU_UNIQUE, and neither RTLD_LOCAL nor DEEPBIND gets out of it). Handing _race a placeholder callable is not an alternative, and T289 measured what actually happens rather than predicting it: the D032 timer REFUSES a block that emits no device kernel (devicetimer.py:344, 'produced no device kernel'), and because _race puts every candidate in ONE session, that exception takes the whole selection session down -- the other candidates lose their measurement too. (R278 section 6.1 predicted a ~0 us candidate being elected as infinitely fast; the direction was right, the mechanism was not -- the timer's guard fires first. R289-data/02-counterfactual.json.) This baseline is measured out of process by baselines._b_tl_mlir.measure_case(); see docs/reports/R278.md. MEASURED ELSEWHERE, NOT MISSING: docs/reports/R282-data/22-timing-summary.json (34 cases x N=5 cross-process, D032 timer, bias band 3.2051%) and docs/reports/R278-data/07-summary.json (26 cases x N=5); the driver is docs/reports/R282-data/scripts/time282.py, which calls baselines._b_tl_mlir.measure_case() directly. This entry's own gate verdict is: R282 G1 PASS 1/2 -- bf16 passes, fp16 misses by 4 float16 ulps (their low-precision route). TO PUT IT IN THE POOL, adapters/handwritten.py would need a candidate that carries a device_us measured in another process; today _race() times every candidate itself in the caller's session (adapters/handwritten.py:215-247) and there is no channel for a pre-measured one. See R289.md divergence 1.

property.value: tilelang-mlir-ascend: RopeNeoxFwdOp/rope_llama31_sf1 (intent=example, kernel=examples/posembedding/rope_llama31/rope_llama31.py): tilelang-mlir-ascend cannot be raced in-process: its Python package is also called `tilelang` and its build/libtilelang.so shares our soname, so importing it here would either shadow or collide with the tilelang that compiled the tested side (D042/R272 -- STB_GNU_UNIQUE, and neither RTLD_LOCAL nor DEEPBIND gets out of it). Handing _race a placeholder callable is not an alternative, and T289 measured what actually happens rather than predicting it: the D032 timer REFUSES a block that emits no device kernel (devicetimer.py:344, 'produced no device kernel'), and because _race puts every candidate in ONE session, that exception takes the whole selection session down -- the other candidates lose their measurement too. (R278 section 6.1 predicted a ~0 us candidate being elected as infinitely fast; the direction was right, the mechanism was not -- the timer's guard fires first. R289-data/02-counterfactual.json.) This baseline is measured out of process by baselines._b_tl_mlir.measure_case(); see docs/reports/R278.md. MEASURED ELSEWHERE, NOT MISSING: docs/reports/R282-data/22-timing-summary.json (34 cases x N=5 cross-process, D032 timer, bias band 3.2051%) and docs/reports/R278-data/07-summary.json (26 cases x N=5); the driver is docs/reports/R282-data/scripts/time282.py, which calls baselines._b_tl_mlir.measure_case() directly. This entry's own gate verdict is: R282 G1 PASS 1/3 -- same fp16 rotation limit. TO PUT IT IN THE POOL, adapters/handwritten.py would need a candidate that carries a device_us measured in another process; today _race() times every candidate itself in the caller's session (adapters/handwritten.py:215-247) and there is no channel for a pre-measured one. See R289.md divergence 1.

This entry's own gate verdict is: R282 G1 PASS 2/2. TO PUT IT IN THE POOL, adapters/handwritten.py would need a candidate that carries a device_us measured in another process; today _race() times every candidate itself in the caller's session (adapters/handwritten.py:215-247) and there is no channel for a pre-measured one. See R289.md divergence 1.

(R278 section 6.1 predicted a ~0 us candidate being elected as infinitely fast; the direction was right, the mechanism was not -- the timer's guard fires first. R289-data/02-counterfactual.json.) This baseline is measured out of process by baselines._b_tl_mlir.measure_case(); see docs/reports/R278.md. MEASURED ELSEWHERE, NOT MISSING: docs/reports/R282-data/22-timing-summary.json (34 cases x N=5 cross-process, D032 timer, bias band 3.2051%) and docs/reports/R278-data/07-summary.json (26 cases x N=5); the driver is docs/reports/R282-data/scripts/time282.py, which calls baselines._b_tl_mlir.measure_case() directly. This entry's own gate verdict is: R282 G1 PASS 2/2 (max_rel 1.14e-3, atol=rtol=1e-3). TO PUT IT IN THE POOL, adapters/handwritten.py would need a candidate that carries a device_us measured in another process; today _race() times every candidate itself in the caller's session (adapters/handwritten.py:215-247) and there is no channel for a pre-measured one. See R289.md divergence 1.

Handing _race a placeholder callable is not an alternative, and T289 measured what actually happens rather than predicting it: the D032 timer REFUSES a block that emits no device kernel (devicetimer.py:344, 'produced no device kernel'), and because _race puts every candidate in ONE session, that exception takes the whole selection session down -- the other candidates lose their measurement too. (R278 section 6.1 predicted a ~0 us candidate being elected as infinitely fast; the direction was right, the mechanism was not -- the timer's guard fires first. R289-data/02-counterfactual.json.) This baseline is measured out of process by baselines._b_tl_mlir.measure_case(); see docs/reports/R278.md. MEASURED ELSEWHERE, NOT MISSING: docs/reports/R282-data/22-timing-summary.json (34 cases x N=5 cross-process, D032 timer, bias band 3.2051%) and docs/reports/R278-data/07-summary.json (26 cases x N=5); the driver is docs/reports/R282-data/scripts/time282.py, which calls baselines._b_tl_mlir.measure_case() directly. This entry's own gate verdict is: 🚨 R282 G1 FAIL 0/1 -- max_abs 0.015625 vs atol=1e-3, guards clean: their whole chain is fp16, our golden has an fp32 intermediate. A numerical-contract miss, NOT a defect. TO PUT IT IN THE POOL, adapters/handwritten.py would need a candidate that carries a device_us measured in another process; today _race() times every candidate itself in the caller's session (adapters/handwritten.py:215-247) and there is no channel for a pre-measured one. See R289.md divergence 1.

property.name: baseline_refused
property.value: tilelang-ascend: block_M=4 with VEC_NUM=2 gives 2 lane(s) in this kernel's per-row statistic buffer, below the measured floor of 8: an Ascend vector instruction addresses whole 32-byte blocks, so a shorter operand encodes a zero-block repeat and the core raises `aicore exception 507015 ... fftsplus aivector error`. Measured for examples/softmax/example_online_softmax.py::online_softmax in docs/reports/R337-data/probe/online-softmax-sweep/summary.tsv (lanes 1/2/4 fault, lanes 8 correct); the same constant our own kernels carry as ROW_EXTENT_GRAIN=8 (R200). Re-fitting it would need the statistics padded to 8 lanes independently of how many rows a lane owns -- a change to the example, not a tile choice (G4); tilelang-mlir-ascend: SoftmaxFwdOp/autotune_2d (intent=unit_test, kernel=testing/autotune/softmax/softmax_2d.py): tilelang-mlir-ascend cannot be raced in-process: its Python package is also called `tilelang` and its build/libtilelang.so shares our soname, so importing it here would either shadow or collide with the tilelang that compiled the tested side (D042/R272 -- STB_GNU_UNIQUE, and neither RTLD_LOCAL nor DEEPBIND gets out of it). Handing _race a placeholder callable is not an alternative, and T289 measured what actually happens rather than predicting it: the D032 timer REFUSES a block that emits no device kernel (devicetimer.py:344, 'produced no device kernel'), and because _race puts every candidate in ONE session, that exception takes the whole selection session down -- the other candidates lose their measurement too. (R278 section 6.1 predicted a ~0 us candidate being elected as infinitely fast; the direction was right, the mechanism was not -- the timer's guard fires first. R289-data/02-counterfactual.json.) This baseline is measured out of process by baselines._b_tl_mlir.measure_case(); see docs/reports/R278.md. MEASURED ELSEWHERE, NOT MISSING: docs/reports/R282-data/22-timing-summary.json (34 cases x N=5 cross-process, D032 timer, bias band 3.2051%) and docs/reports/R278-data/07-summary.json (26 cases x N=5); the driver is docs/reports/R282-data/scripts/time282.py, which calls baselines._b_tl_mlir.measure_case() directly. This entry's own gate verdict is: R282 G1 PASS 1/1 (max_rel 2.70e-7; fp32 2-D case only -- the 3-D cases reduce dim=0, see R282 B4). TO PUT IT IN THE POOL, adapters/handwritten.py would need a candidate that carries a device_us measured in another process; today _race() times every candidate itself in the caller's session (adapters/handwritten.py:215-247) and there is no channel for a pre-measured one. See R289.md divergence 1.

property.value: ops-transformer-b1: TopkSelectorFwdOp is a masked top-k over a [B, S, Skv, G] fp32 score with a per-row [starts, ends) window, Skv = 65536 and topk = 1024/2048. All three candidates are eliminated by measurement (R253-data/indexing-candidates.json, R253-data/topk-manifest-shape.json): (1) aclnnMoeGatingTopK (tr_b2) -- last axis hard-limited to 2048: 2048 ok, 2049 returns 561002; (2) aclnnMoeGatingTopKSoftmax (tr_b1) -- reaches 65536, but it FUSES the normalization: for x=[3,1,2,0] it returns [0.6439, 0.2369], which is softmax(x) at indices 0 and 2, not the raw scores; our operator is handed an already-computed score and must not renormalize. It also has no mask/start/end input, so the [starts, ends) window -- the whole point of the operator -- cannot be expressed, and k = 2048 returns 561002 at Skv = 65536 (k = 1024 is the ceiling); (3) ops-math radix_top_k -- listed among the 41 ops with an ascend910b config, but it has no op_host/op_api directory at all, so it exports no aclnn entry point (ops-math's libcust_opapi.so exports 8 aclnn symbols, none of them top-k), and it is not among the 9 operators built into opp_math_b3. It would need both a new build and a new API layer. coverage_status = public_handwritten_gap
